author_reading_scope: Inspected the complete relevant sections in three full-text sources. Sutton and Barto: Chapter 8 §§8.1–8.3 and §§8.5–8.7, including finite model conventions, deterministic last-observation Dyna-Q, experienced-pair planning, model exploitation, and planning backups; the accessible PDF contains only an §8.8 MCTS heading, so no MCTS claim is used. Levine et al.: full §2.1 and §§5.1–5.3, including finite-horizon expected-return conventions, distribution shift, model exploitation, ensemble disagreement limitations, and short-rollout context. Barto et al.: §§4.1, 5.1–5.3, 6.1–6.2, Theorem 3, and complete Appendix A. The local SSP/value and asynchronous convergence proofs are complete; direct inspection of the source RTDP theorem/proof was followed by a counterexample satisfying its stated hypotheses, so the theorem is not accepted as a valid supplier.

item_reading.claim: Defines finite true and learned reward/transition tables on a common state-action domain; reward errors are absolute expected-reward errors and transition errors are half-l1/TV errors on an explicit pair set, with empty-set maximum zero.
item_reading.argument: Finite probability rows normalize the true and estimated kernels; bounded rewards and finite pairwise errors make all maxima well-defined.

item_reading.claim: Defines finite SSP goals as absorbing zero-reward dummy actions, expected nonglobal costs with a common positive lower bound, and properness by finite-prefix survival probabilities.
item_reading.argument: Finite transition and policy rows make every survival recursion term well-defined in [0,1].

item_reading.claim: Defines time-dependent Markov policies, finite occupancy recursion, and undiscounted H-step expected return.
item_reading.argument: Induction proves each occupancy vector is a probability law; rewards in [0,1] imply the return lies in [0,H].

item_reading.claim: Specifies exact-model undiscounted RTDP with current-state greedy backups, fresh uniform tie draws, finite trial cap, and supplied recurring starts, without a standalone convergence guarantee.
item_reading.argument: The routine is procedural; its trial boundary and tie rule are explicit inputs for later hypothesis checking.

item_reading.claim: Under a fixed finite Markov policy, the next-state TV distance is at most the current distance plus the learned-occupancy-weighted uniform row error.
item_reading.argument: Apply common-kernel contraction, bound the policy-mixture perturbation by the weighted rowwise half-l1 errors, then use the triangle inequality.

item_reading.claim: For a finite positive-cost SSP with a proper stationary policy, the optimal total cost is finite, attained by a proper deterministic stationary policy, and is the unique finite nonnegative Bellman fixed point.
item_reading.argument: Finite-horizon Bellman minima increase and are bounded by a block-geometric cost bound for the supplied proper policy; passage to the limit gives a fixed point; greedy finite choices are proper by positive-cost growth; Bellman inequalities establish optimality and uniqueness.

axiom_uses.reason: Invokes Ionescu–Tulcea only for the full trajectory law of a history-dependent policy; finite action choices use induction.

item_reading.claim: Defines mean pairwise TV disagreement for a finite ensemble and states that dispersion alone does not specify a true-error probability law or calibrated coverage frequency.
item_reading.argument: The distinction is definitional; no calibration guarantee is asserted.

item_reading.claim: Specifies tabular Dyna-Q with deterministic last-observation model, real Q-learning update, and planning only on previously experienced pairs.
item_reading.argument: The exact stored transition is justified only for deterministic environments and already observed pairs; no convergence guarantee is claimed.

item_reading.claim: Specifies finite-horizon Bellman planning in a learned model and returns the first action before replanning after one real transition.
item_reading.argument: The finite recursion and deterministic tie listing define a finite procedure; no true-return guarantee is claimed.

item_reading.claim: Defines off-support model exploitation relative to a finite policy class by positive learned occupancy off the data support, strict own-return overprediction, and strict true suboptimality.
item_reading.argument: Finite return values and a finite nonempty policy class make both maxima attained; all predicates are comparisons over finite tables.

item_reading.claim: For one fixed finite-horizon Markov policy, common initial law, and reachable-pair errors epsilon_r and epsilon_p, the return difference is at most H epsilon_r + binom(H,2) epsilon_p.
item_reading.argument: TV state-law error grows by at most epsilon_p per step; the time-t reward mismatch is bounded by t epsilon_p plus epsilon_r; summing gives the claimed coefficient.

item_reading.claim: From a finite initial value table below f*, zero on goals, asynchronous exact Bellman backups of every nonglobal state infinitely often converge uniformly to f* in a finite positive-cost SSP.
item_reading.argument: The maximum error is nonincreasing; a hypothetical positive limiting error induces a non-goal closed set of Bellman-optimal actions and forces costs to grow by at least c_min per step, contradicting finite f*.

item_reading.claim: Refutes the general optimal-relevant-state RTDP convergence claim under the source-stated non-overestimating initialization and tie conditions.
item_reading.argument: In a five-state SSP, two actions at the start have equal true cost, but the visited branch value approaches the optimum strictly from below; the alternative optimal action is never greedy and its downstream state estimate stays incorrect. Costs f and reward values V are related by V=-f, so the source condition V0≥V* is met by the specified f0≤f* table.
sources: Barto et al. Theorem 3 and Appendix A
item_reading.source_disposition: The source theorem is the claim being tested and contradicted; it is not used as a valid proof supplier.

item_reading.claim: An inaccurate off-support model yields the exact return for a fixed policy whose reachable pairs are modeled exactly.
item_reading.argument: Reachable reward and transition errors are zero, so the fixed-policy simulation theorem gives zero return discrepancy.

item_reading.claim: A one-state horizon-one learned optimizer selects an unsupported action with predicted return 1 and true return 0 although the supported action returns 1/2.
item_reading.argument: Direct enumeration of the two deterministic policies verifies learned optimality, off-support occupancy, overprediction, and true suboptimality.

item_reading.claim: A two-state exact-reward model with transition error epsilon has discrepancy sum_{t=0}^{H-1}(1-(1-epsilon)^t) under the sole policy.
item_reading.argument: State occupancy at the safe state is (1-epsilon)^t in the learned model and 1 in the true model; the exact return difference satisfies the fixed-policy bound.
